land.text: 'The West Saxons succeeded in conquering Sussex (hitherto under direct Mercian rule), Kent, and Essex' after Ellendun, September 825

successors.note: The Kent infobox gives 'Full integration into crown of Wessex: 825'. Cliopatria ends its Kent row in 762, when its Mercia row takes Kent over (763).

capitals.name: Canterbury
capitals.note: The page names no capital. It says 'Canterbury grew into the economic and political centre of Kent during the seventh century' and that Canterbury and Rochester 'were the home to major mints'; royal halls are named at Eastry (c. 664-667) and Lundenwic (until the 680s). Canterbury is shown throughout as the later centre; nothing on the page places a seat earlier.

correction.text: Kent as Cliopatria draws it from 490, extended back to the c. 455 foundation

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's Kent row begins in 490, but the infobox says 'Established: c. 455' (Anglo-Saxon Chronicle: the battle with Vortigern at Ægelesthrep in 455, after which Hengist 'succeeded [Horsa] as king'). The page calls the accounts 'largely mythic' (Barbara Yorke), so the year is conventional. The 490 outline is carried back unchanged.

490-533, 4,349 km2. The infobox gives no area, so the Cliopatria figure cannot be compared; the outline is the modern county of Kent. The page says only that 'East Kent annexed West Kent' in an undated sixth century, so before that the kingdom may have been the eastern half; the page is silent on the year and the shape stands.

534-691, 4,063 km2. The infobox gives no area, so the Cliopatria figure cannot be compared; the outline is the modern county of Kent. From c. 604 to 616 Kent is overlord of Essex (ledger). Inside these years Kent is conquered by Cædwalla (686), revolts (687), is Mercian-backed under Oswine (688) and shares west Kent with an East Saxon king (689-692); the ledger carries these as occupation and vassal events over an outline that does not change. Wessex defeated Kentish forces in 568 and pushed them back into Kent.

correction.text: Kent under Wihtred, 692-704: the 705 outline carried back; the page notes Wihtred 'may have ceded some border territory to Ine' in 694 but gives no place

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Kent shape for 692-704, yet Wihtred reigned throughout ('by 694 Wihtred was the sole ruler of Kent'; he died on 23 April 725). The 705 outline is used for the gap.
705-717, 4,086 km2. Wihtred's reign; nothing on the page changes the outline. The infobox gives no area, so the Cliopatria figure cannot be compared; the outline is the modern county of Kent.

718-740, 4,063 km2. After Wihtred's death in 725 'two or even three kings typically ruled simultaneously' for forty years; the kingdom is divided among kings, not in land lost. The infobox gives no area, so the Cliopatria figure cannot be compared; the outline is the modern county of Kent.

741-754, 4,217 km2 (3.8 percent above the neighbouring shapes; Cliopatria noise, the page records no gain). The infobox gives no area, so the Cliopatria figure cannot be compared; the outline is the modern county of Kent.
755-756, 4,063 km2; same outline as 718. The infobox gives no area, so the Cliopatria figure cannot be compared; the outline is the modern county of Kent.

757-762, 4,063 km2. Cliopatria ends the row in 762 and its Kingdom of Mercia shape grows in 763; the page has Kent a separate kingdom with its own kings until 825 under Mercian supremacy from 764. The infobox gives no area, so the Cliopatria figure cannot be compared; the outline is the modern county of Kent.

correction.text: Kent as in 757-762, kept as a separate kingdom until the West Saxons annexed it in 825; vassal of Mercia 764-776, 785-796 and 798-825

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Kent continues 763-825 under its own kings, but under Mercian supremacy for most of these years ('764: Offa gained supremacy over Kent'; independent 776-785 and 796-798). The 757 outline is kept and the ledger's vassal events set the tint; the Kingdom of Mercia dossier carries the mirror events.

ledger.note: c. 455: Hengist, then his son Æsc, found the kingdom of Kent. Infobox 'Established: c. 455'; the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle puts the battle with Vortigern at Ægelesthrep in 455 and says 'Horsa was killed' and 'Hengist succeeded him as king, followed in turn by his son [Æsc]'. Scholars treat Hengist and Horsa as mythological, so the year is a convention.

region.text: Essex: the counties of Essex, Middlesex and much of Hertfordshire

ledger.note: c. 604: Æthelberht of Kent becomes overlord of Essex. The Essex page: Æthelberht 'was in a position to exercise some authority in Essex shortly after 604' as Sæberht's overlord; the Æthelberht page has Bede listing him third among the kings with imperium, and says Bede's account of Rædwald of East Anglia is unclear. Suzerain's record: the counterpart is the vassal.

region.text: Essex: the counties of Essex, Middlesex and much of Hertfordshire

ledger.note: 616: Kentish overlordship over Essex lapses. Sæberht died in 616 ('After the death of Sæberht in 616, Mellitus was driven out') and Æthelberht on 24 February 616; the Æthelberht page says only that Eadbald's revolt 'may have been a reaction to Kentish overlordship after Æthelberht's death' and does not say when it ended. A bridge.
686: Cædwalla of Wessex conquers Kent. 'In 686 Kent was conquered by Cædwalla of Wessex'; the Cædwalla page adds that 'He installed his brother, Mul, as king of Kent, in place of its king Eadric'.

c. 687: Kent revolts and Mul is burned. 'Within a year, his brother Mul was killed in a Kentish revolt, and Cædwalla returned to devastate the kingdom'; the Cædwalla page dates Mul's burning c. 687 (Anglo-Saxon Chronicle) and has Cædwalla abdicating in 688.

688: Oswine takes the Kentish throne with Mercian backing. 'Oswine, who was probably supported by Æthelred of Mercia, took the throne for a time'; the Kent page: 'Mercians backed client king Oswine, who seems to have reigned for only about two years'. Recorded from the vassal's side: the counterpart is the overlord.

region.text: West Kent (Rochester and the Thames side); the page gives no boundary

ledger.note: 689: East Saxon kings are active in west Kent. '689-690: East Saxon kings under Mercian overlordship were active in West Kent'; the Wihtred page has Swæfheard, son of Sebbi of Essex, king in west Kent while Oswine held east Kent. The page gives no boundary between the halves.

c. 691: Wihtred succeeds in Kent (charter evidence 'April to July 691'; Bede's length of reign would give late 690) and Oswine's Mercian-backed kingship ends. The page does not say that Mercian overlordship stopped; recorded as a bridge.

region.text: West Kent (Rochester and the Thames side); the page gives no boundary

ledger.note: 692: the East Saxon kingship in west Kent ends. Wihtred 'initially shared power with Swæfheard, who is last mentioned in July 692', and 'by 694 Wihtred was the sole ruler of Kent'; the page does not say how it ended, so this is a bridge.

764: Offa of Mercia gains supremacy over Kent. '764: Offa gained supremacy over Kent'; the Offa page shows a charter of that year in which Offa granted land at Rochester in his own name with Heahberht witnessing as king of Kent. Kent keeps its kings.

776: the Kentish rebels seem to win at Otford. 'Battle of Otford; the outcome is unknown, but the rebels seem to have prevailed. Egbert II and Ealhmund then ruled independently for nearly a decade.' The Offa page says the Chronicle gives no outcome, that tradition reads a Mercian victory, and that a 784 charter naming only Ealhmund suggests a Mercian loss. [Reviewer eu-11-b: the Kent infobox status line gives 'Client state of Mercia (764–769, 785–796, 798–825)' and 'Independent kingdom (... 769–785 ...)', so the infobox ends this client period in 769, not 776; 776 follows the page text (Otford) and is kept at confidence 2.]

785: Offa re-establishes his authority over Kent. 'Offa firmly re-established his authority over Kent in 785'; the Offa page has him treating Kent 'as an ordinary province of the Mercian kingdom' in 785-789.
796: Eadberht Præn restores Kentish independence after Offa's death. 'Kentish rebellion under Eadbert Praen temporarily succeeded after Offa's death'; Offa died on 29 July 796 (Offa page).

798: Coenwulf of Mercia reconquers Kent and installs Cuthred. 'Coenwulf reconquered Kent and installed Cuthred. Cuthred died in 807, after which Coenwulf ruled directly.' The page does not date the end of direct Mercian rule before Baldred, a client king expelled in 825, so the vassal status is kept to 825.

825: the Mercian grip on Kent ends at Ellendun. The battle was fought 'between Ecgberht of Wessex and Beornwulf of Mercia in September 825'; the Kent page: 'Mercian authority was replaced by that of Wessex', and the client king Baldred was expelled.

region.text: Kent, annexed by Wessex after Ellendun

ledger.note: 825: Wessex annexes Kent. Ecgberht sent his son Æthelwulf into the south-east, and 'The West Saxons succeeded in conquering Sussex (hitherto under direct Mercian rule), Kent, and Essex', annexed to Wessex and 'roughly doubling its size'. Kent infobox: 'Full integration into crown of Wessex: 825'.

wars.name: Kentish-West Saxon battle of 568
wars.outcome: Æthelberht's forces were pushed back into Kent; no land changed hands.
wars.note: The page: 'the one exception was a battle between the Kentish and West Saxons in 568'. The Æthelberht page has the Chronicle at Wibbandun: 'Æthelberht lost the battle and was driven back to Kent', but calls Ceawlin's dates unreliable and suggests c. 590.

wars.name: Mercian invasion of Kent (676)
wars.outcome: Æthelred of Mercia ravaged Kent; no land changed hands on the page.
wars.note: Added by reviewer eu-11-b. The Kent page: 'in 676 the Mercian king' Æthelred 'led an attack that destroyed many Kentish churches'. Zones empty: the page records no territorial change.

wars.name: Cædwalla's conquest of Kent
wars.outcome: Cædwalla installed his brother Mul in 686; the Kentish burned Mul c. 687 and Cædwalla devastated the land; in 694 Wihtred 'made peace with the West Saxon king Ine' by paying compensation for Mul (the Chronicle manuscripts give 'thirty thousand').
wars.note: The Wihtred page adds that Wihtred 'may have ceded some border territory to Ine' in 694; no place is named, so the outline is unchanged.

wars.name: Mercian war against Kent (Otford)
wars.outcome: The Anglo-Saxon Chronicle: 'the Mercians and the inhabitants of Kent fought at Otford'; the outcome is not recorded. The rebels seem to have prevailed (Kent page); tradition says a Mercian victory (Offa page). Kent was independent 776-785.
wars.note: Offa had tried to rule Kent directly in the early 770s, which provoked the rebellion (Kent page). No contest event: the ledger's vassal pairs carry the status.

wars.name: Kentish revolt and Mercian reconquest
wars.outcome: Eadberht Præn's rebellion succeeded after Offa's death in 796; in 798 Coenwulf reconquered Kent and installed Cuthred.

wars.name: West Saxon conquest of the south-east (Ellendun)
wars.outcome: Ecgberht beat Beornwulf at Ellendun in September 825; Æthelwulf then took Kent, Sussex and Essex for Wessex.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line is on any page opened: the frontiers are the sea, the Thames estuary and the Weald, drawn approximately; the division of west and east Kent is undated and unbounded.

notes: Cliopatria's Kent row ends 762 and its Mercia shape grows in 763 and 772; this dossier instead keeps Kent a separate kingdom to 825 (the page's own date for full integration into Wessex) and records Mercian supremacy as vassal pairs. The Kingdom of Mercia dossier must carry the mirror vassal_start/vassal_end pairs (764, 776, 785, 796, 798, 825) with counterpart kingdom-of-kent, or the two will draw Kent twice; the Wessex dossier the 686 occupation and the 825 gain. The page gives no infobox area, so the area check could not be done. Not placed on a year: the undated annexation of West Kent by East Kent in the sixth century, and Æthelberht's wider overlordship ('controlled everything south of the River Humber', late sixth century); the overlordship over East Anglia (Rædwald) rests on a Bede passage the Æthelberht page calls unclear, so only the Essex overlordship (604-616) is dated. After 725 'two or even three kings' ruled together, which changes no outline. The Kent page's last-king line (Æthelred, 866-871) is not reconciled with the 825 integration date. Native names: none recorded on the pages opened.
